summary: The weakest batch of the campaign so far, and it reads as written tired. Commons and most Uncommons are fine small habits (the drain-seeking ball, the hedge, the cork in the piggy bank, the dice that never rolls a six), but from Rare upwards most objects simply do their job: the racket smashes, the shin guard stops kicks, the pacifier calms, the teether is chewed, the starting block launches. About 60 Rares have no troublesome power and no punchline. About 45 Epics are the same crowd frame ('was X-ed by every child / player / guest at the Y, and the whole Z ...'), and the Legendaries split into sports wins and records (about 15), generations and endurance ('four generations', 'for fifty years', 'never leaked once', about 12) and quiet successes with no joke. 'The X That Y' is the shape of 75 of the 85 Legendary names. There are copy-paste clusters: the only tree on the beach / in the park (kite, boomerang), the roof (ball, tennis ball, shuttlecock), the drain / gutter (ball, bowling ball), the shot from the other end of the court (basketball, handball), and the baby cluster (bottle, pacifier, teether, rattle, music box, mobile) all ending in sleeping babies or generations. x_rocking_toy repeats w17's rocking horse. About 20 Ultimates that change effect per variant carry a heat, flash or stink word. Safety: the pool float rider asleep drifting across a lake, toddlers tasting play dough, a dodgeball aimed at heads. Replacements and paired names are given for every high and medium item; the w16 Rares, Epics and Legendaries need a near-complete rewrite, and the replacements below supply one.

patterns.pattern: Rare = the object doing its job well (no troublesome power, no punchline): racket smashes, shin guard stops kicks, knee pads soften falls, elbow pads save elbows, pacifier calms, teether gets chewed, starting block launches, sticker goes on the chart, flippers make you fast.
patterns.suggestion: Each Rare below is replaced with a power that causes trouble (the dice that always finds the longest snake, the boomerang that follows its thrower into the bath, the mouthguard that turns words into sneezes).

patterns.pattern: Crowd-scene Epics: 'was used by every X at the Y (at once), and the whole Z ...' with no joke beyond the crowd.
patterns.suggestion: Replace with one concrete consequence and a joke (the bus driver turning on the wipers for the rattle, the pinata's lollipops in next door's guttering, the dog striped like a tiger by the crayon box).

patterns.pattern: Sports-win and record Legendaries: won the final, scored the winning goal, broke the school record, perfect game, made every shot.
patterns.suggestion: Each needs an outrageous feat with a punchline instead (the shot put landing in next year's sports day, the softball landing in another time zone).

patterns.pattern: Generations and endurance Legendaries: 'four generations', 'for fifty years without', 'never leaked once', 'for a hundred years', 'a thousand falls'.
Legendary name monotony: 75 of 85 are 'The X That/Who Y' or 'The X of Y'.
patterns.suggestion: New Legendary names below use 'Name the Epithet', 'Name, the Epithet', titles and puns; about ten 'The X That Y' names are left where they still read well.

patterns.pattern: Copy-paste premises across objects: the only tree on the beach / in the park (kite C, boomerang U); the roof (ball L, tennis ball R, shuttlecock U); rolling straight into the drain / gutter (ball C, bowling ball C); a shot from the other end of the court in the final (basketball L, handball L); generations of babies (rattle, music box, pacifier, teether, tea set, rocking toy); lullaby sleep (music box R/E/L, mobile toy E/L).
patterns.suggestion: One owner keeps each premise; the others are replaced below.

patterns.pattern: Cross-batch duplicate: x_rocking_toy (looks like a horse) repeats w17 x_rocking_horse (galloping across the room, rocked by generations).
patterns.suggestion: x_rocking_toy is rewritten here (biscuit creeping, seasick goldfish, the house that rocks); w17's rocking horse keeps the galloping.

patterns.pattern: Ultimates whose effect varies by variant carry a heat, flash or stink word that is wrong for at least one variant (Gallop Heat, Top Corner Heat, Home Run Heat, Wig Swap Flash, Double Six Flash, Game Over Pong, Leaky Bag Pong and others).

Names that describe a different line or repeat another rarity: baby bottle Midnightfeed (R) / Midnight Feed (E); handheld 'Cardigan Pocket'; dino 'Roarbutton' on the nodding head; checkers 'Doublejump' on the crowning line; dice 'Tableroller'; medicine ball U 'Floorthud' (repeats C); pacifier 'Pramthrower' on the hiding line; marble 'Cleverlosesit' (garbled).
Templated 'the whole X' phrasing in about 40 lines ('wakes the whole house', 'the whole sleepover goes quiet', 'the whole beach whirred', 'the whole street came out').
patterns.suggestion: Most go with the rewrites; keep it to one or two in the batch.

patterns.pattern: Several Commons and Uncommons are under 60 characters (Outsideline 33, Fuzzlost 30, Wristsoaker 37, Sockstuffer 37). They are acceptable habits but would land better with a small consequence.
